citation: Corrales M., Hoteit L., Ravasi M. (2024). Seis2Rock: A Data-Driven Approach to Direct Petrophysical Inversion of Pre-Stack Seismic Data. Earth and Space Science 11, e2023EA003301. DOI:10.1029/2023EA003301 (arXiv:2307.07969)
problem: Direct petrophysical inversion from prestack AVO
forward_physics: SVD-derived optimal basis of Zoeppritz reflectivity (linear, background-subtracted)
main_contribution: Physics-derived optimal linear basis needs only 1 well to define projection; band-limited regularized post-stack-style inversion of petrophysical reflectivities
limitations: Linear/SVD-truncated; single synthetic case; no uncertainty; matched forward physics (inverse crime by construction since basis is derived from the same Zoeppritz generator)
difference_from_proposed_research: This is the direct baseline our RW-PGNN work already benchmarks against. No uncertainty, no resolvability framing, no field test.

citation: Das V., Mukerji T. (2020). Petrophysical properties prediction from pre-stack seismic data using convolutional neural networks (PetroNet). Geophysics 85(5), N41-N55. DOI:10.1190/geo2019-0650.1
dataset: Synthetic + field (Netherlands F3-type or similar; check original paper for exact field)
forward_physics: None explicit in end-to-end PetroNet; physics only in cascaded ElasticNet/ElasticPetroNet split
field_validation: Not confirmed from search alone (verify against original paper)
main_contribution: Established that direct end-to-end CNNs can outperform physics-constrained cascades in-distribution; introduced MC Dropout for epistemic UQ in this problem class
limitations: Authors themselves note MC Dropout underestimates true uncertainty; aleatoric uncertainty not modeled; no explicit resolvability analysis
difference_from_proposed_research: Existing notebooks already use this as a comparison baseline (PetroNet/Cascaded). No forward-model-mismatch or resolvability analysis in the original paper.

citation: Vashisth D., Mukerji T. (2022). Direct Estimation of Porosity from Seismic Data using Rock and Wave Physics Informed Neural Networks (RW-PINN). The Leading Edge 41(12), 840-846. DOI:10.1190/tle41120840.1 (arXiv:2210.00042)
dataset: Synthetic (uncemented sand rock physics model) + limited real wells
problem: Weakly-supervised direct porosity estimation from few wells
forward_physics: Uncemented-sand rock physics model + NORMAL-INCIDENCE (poststack, not angle-dependent) wave physics
field_validation: Partial (weak/limited wells used as supervision; not a held-out blind-well test framed as validation)
blind_wells: No formal blind-well protocol reported in the abstract-level description
main_contribution: Coined the 'rock- and wave-physics-informed neural network' (RW-PINN) paradigm: few-well weak supervision + physics-consistency loss for direct petrophysical estimation
limitations: Single property (porosity only); normal-incidence (no AVA/angle information); non-uniqueness handled only via weighted NRMSE loss, not distributional UQ
difference_from_proposed_research: CRITICAL OVERLAP: this paper already establishes the RW-PINN/RW-PGNN naming and paradigm (rock+wave physics informed NN, few-well weak supervision). Our RW-PGNN differs in (a) multi-property (phi,Vsh,Sw) vs porosity-only, (b) full prestack AVA/exact Zoeppritz forward model vs normal-incidence, (c) well-count scaling + spatially-buffered leakage-aware validation. These are the ONLY defensible differences from this direct precedent and must be stated explicitly, not implied as new.

citation: Li P., Liu M., Alfarraj M., Tahmasebi P., Grana D. (2024). Probabilistic physics-informed neural network for seismic petrophysical inversion (P-PINN). Geophysics 89(2), M17-M32. DOI:10.1190/geo2023-0214.1
dataset: Synthetic + North Sea field (poststack and prestack)
forward_physics: PINN with a reparameterization network + rock-physics-model hyperparameter estimation network
properties_predicted: Petrophysical properties (paper predicts porosity/lithology-type properties; verify exact list against full text)
uncertainty_considered: Yes - Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) for model/parameter uncertainty
property_specific_resolvability_consider: which is one source of forward-model uncertainty)
main_contribution: Not confirmed whether formal held-out blind well used (verify against full text)
limitations: First PINN for seismic petrophysical inversion with an explicit probabilistic/ABC treatment of rock-physics-model uncertainty, validated on field data
difference_from_proposed_research: ABC does not directly separate aleatoric vs epistemic uncertainty in the reservoir-property predictions themselves; no explicit calibration/reliability-diagram analysis reported in available abstract; no explicit multi-uncertainty-source degradation study
column15: MAJOR OVERLAP with proposed Objective 3/Paper 2: 'probabilistic physics-guided petrophysical inversion with uncertainty' already exists, published in Geophysics, WITH field validation (which our existing RW-PGNN work lacks entirely). Our contribution must be narrower: property-specific resolvability tied explicitly to AVA information degradation, calibration diagnostics (coverage, CRPS, confident-error rate), and controlled multi-source uncertainty stress-testing (velocity/RMO, wavelet, amplitude/noise) rather than only rock-physics-hyperparameter uncertainty.

citation: Li P., Grana D., Liu M. (2024). Bayesian neural network and Bayesian physics-informed neural network via variational inference for seismic petrophysical inversion (BPINN-VI). Geophysics 89(6), M185-M196. DOI:10.1190/geo2023-0737.1
dataset: Synthetic prestack + North Sea field (oil-saturated clastic reservoir)
problem: Variational-inference Bayesian PINN for petrophysical inversion
forward_physics: Physics-dependent loss term embedding petrophysical-to-seismic relations
properties_predicted: Petrophysical properties (verify exact list against full text)
uncertainty_considered: Yes - variational inference (weight-space posterior over the network)
main_contribution: Demonstrates BPINN-VI outperforms plain BNN-VI (higher R^2/correlation, lower uncertainty, better lateral continuity) on both synthetic and field prestack data
limitations: VI posteriors are known to underestimate multimodality/tail uncertainty relative to full MCMC or ensembles; no explicit forward-model-mismatch stress test reported
difference_from_proposed_research: Same overlap concern as the P-PINN paper above (same lead authors, same general problem): a published, field-validated, uncertainty-aware physics-guided seismic petrophysical inversion method already exists. Differentiate on resolvability framing and controlled uncertainty-source degradation, not on 'probabilistic PGNN' alone.

citation: Wu S., Wang Y., Li Q., He Z., Geng J. (2024). Joint data-driven and physics-driven prestack amplitude-variation-with-angle elastic parameter inversion. Geophysics 89(1), 17-32. DOI:10.1190/geo2023-0135.1
problem: Joint physics-constrained + automatic-differentiation AVA elastic inversion
forward_physics: Physics-constrained NN (PCNN) and automatic-differentiation-based forward AVA modeling
properties_predicted: Elastic parameters (Vp/Vs/rho or Ip/Is-type; NOT direct petrophysical phi/Vsh/Sw - verify)
uncertainty_considered: No explicit UQ reported in search snippet (verify)
main_contribution: Introduces two complementary deep-learning AVA elastic inversion routes (physics-constrained network vs. autodiff-based) and compares them
limitations: Targets elastic properties, not direct petrophysical properties; no explicit resolvability or uncertainty-calibration study reported
difference_from_proposed_research: Adjacent but not directly overlapping: elastic-domain AVA inversion, not multi-property petrophysical inversion with UQ. Relevant as a forward-operator/architecture reference for our Objective 3, not a competing claim to novelty.

citation: Auestad et al. (2025). A Practical and Efficient Approach for Bayesian Seismic AVO Inversion: Insights from the Alvheim Field. Geophysical Prospecting. DOI: verify at onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1365-2478.70108
properties_predicted: Linearized AVO (Aki-Richards/Shuey-type) with Bayesian posterior over elastic parameters
limitations: Demonstrates a computationally practical Bayesian AVO workflow validated on a real North Sea field
difference_from_proposed_research: Elastic-domain, not reservoir-property domain; practicality-focused rather than resolvability-focused
column15: Relevant as a field-validated Bayesian AVO precedent and as a candidate baseline/reference for what a 'practical' probabilistic workflow should look like; not a direct competitor to the petrophysical resolvability question.

citation: Sarkar D., Baumel R.T., Larner K.L. (2002). Velocity analysis in the presence of amplitude variation. Geophysics 67(5), 1664-1672. DOI:10.1190/1.1512814
limitations: Shows AVO gradient errors from velocity/moveout error are proportional to sin^2(theta) and to the time-derivative of the zero-offset trace; velocity errors as small as ~0.2% measurably distort AVO gradient
difference_from_proposed_research: Addresses gradient distortion from velocity error at the AVO-attribute level, not property-resolvability or petrophysical inversion
column15: Directly supports (and should anchor) Objective 2A / 'Study A': the physical mechanism by which velocity/RMO error couples into Shuey gradient error. Our contribution, if any, must be the propagation of this into property-specific resolvability loss, which this paper does not do.

citation: Kennedy M.C., O'Hagan A. (2001). Bayesian calibration of computer models. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 63(3), 425-464.
forward_physics: General: y(x) = eta(x,theta) + delta(x) + epsilon, with delta(x) a Gaussian-process model-form discrepancy
uncertainty_considered: Yes (this IS the foundational discrepancy-modeling framework)
forward_model_mismatch_considered: Yes (this is the origin of 'forward-model mismatch' as a formal statistical object)
main_contribution: Established the standard statistical treatment of the gap between an imperfect simulator/forward model and reality
limitations: Not geophysics-specific; direct GP-discrepancy modeling does not scale trivially to the high-dimensional, structured (per-angle, per-depth) seismic forward-modeling setting
difference_from_proposed_research: Foundational reference for how to FORMALIZE 'forward-model mismatch' (F != F_hat) in Objective 3, rather than treating it only informally as in the existing RW-PGNN notebooks.

citation: Roberts D.R. et al. (2017). Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure. Ecography 40(8), 913-929.
main_contribution: Establishes buffered/blocked spatial cross-validation as the correct way to avoid leakage-inflated performance under spatial autocorrelation
difference_from_proposed_research: Already adopted correctly in the existing GEOP592_RWPGNN_FINAL notebook (Part 2.8 buffered well-count sweep) and in the Seis2Rock_ML_audit notebook (Part 2.6 buffered K-fold). No further novelty claim needed here - this is good existing practice to preserve

citation: Ploton P. et al. (2020). Spatial validation reveals poor predictive performance of large-scale ecological mapping models. Nature Communications 11, 4540.
problem: Demonstrates inflated apparent performance under naive (non-spatial) validation
main_contribution: Empirically demonstrates the magnitude of performance inflation from spatially-naive validation splits
difference_from_proposed_research: Same as Roberts et al. 2017 - already correctly cited and used as motivation for the Part 2.8 buffered-split experiment in the existing RW-PGNN notebook.

citation: Gal Y., Ghahramani Z. (2016). Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning. Proceedings of ICML 2016.
problem: Cheap approximate Bayesian uncertainty via dropout at inference
limitations: Popularized MC Dropout as a practical epistemic-uncertainty proxy for deep networks
difference_from_proposed_research: Approximates only a restricted variational family; known to underestimate true posterior uncertainty and does not capture aleatoric/data-noise uncertainty
column15: Already used in the existing notebooks' Das & Mukerji baseline (MC Dropout). Confirms MC Dropout alone is insufficient for the aleatoric+forward-model-mismatch uncertainty this PhD needs to target - motivates moving beyond it in Objective 3.
